title.narrative: Activity under preparation Pacific Trade and Sustainable Development Programme

description.narrative: The EU Pacific Trade and Sustainable Development Programme will: (1) develop Trade and Sustainable Development (TSD) policy in line with regional, EU-ACP Partnership (Samoa Agreement) and EU-Pacific States interim Economic Partnership Agreements (EPA); (2) strengthen and integrate Pacific export-oriented green and inclusive value chains through international trade instruments and actions; (3) improve the access of Pacific green and accesible goods and services to EU and international markets; (4) identify and design sustainable trade-related investment projects through the EU Global Gateway initiative. The action will aim to contribute to the sustainable, climate-resilient, integrated and inclusive economic development of the Pacific countries of the African Caribbean and Pacific group (PACP), providing economic, social and environmental benefits to communities. The action will support SDG 5 on creating opportunities for women¿s economic empowerment, SDG 8 on decent work and economic growth; SDG 12 on responsible production and consumption; SDG 13 on climate action; and SDG 17 on partnerships for the goals.The action will adopt an integrated and demand-driven approach to address the main trade and sustainability challenges of the region, recognising the diversity of needs and opportunities across the PACP countries, building on the lessons learned from and outcomes of the Pacific Regional Integration Support (PRISE) programme and the Pacific European Union Marine Partnership (PEUMP) Programme 1 and 2, coordinating with other technical and financial partners and complementing other EU programmes in the region. The action will also aim to address the common priorities of the EU and those identified by Pacific Leaders and stakeholders of the region by aligning with the `EU-Pacific Green-Blue alliance¿ which articulates the cross-cutting priorities between the European Green Deal and the Pacific Leaders¿ `2050 Strategy for a Blue Pacific Continent¿. The action will also aim to support the forthcoming regional trade and environment strategy currently under formulation following a mandate by Pacific Ministers in 2023.
